def.title: Abandoned Cache
notes: The free deterministic reward is the old gamble's small result; paying two gold buys the former winning result, so the player chooses certainty rather than a hidden coin flip.
def.body: The trail dips into the Silt Hollows, and there, half-swallowed by mud, a supply crate juts from the muck, its lock long rusted through. Someone left here in a hurry — or never came back at all. Pry it open and it could hold anything worth carrying, or nothing at all but the reason it was abandoned.

def.title: The Banner-Scribe
notes: Board identity begins at three cards sharing one weapon type and is rederived whenever this conditional event is checked, so a detour cannot leave a stale gate. Sketching for a coin keeps the event safely resolvable without a qualifying board.
def.body: A banner-scribe has set her table among the Muster Road's camps, reading fighters' colors off their gear the way other scribes read letters. One look over your board and she is already mixing paint: if you march under a device, she knows a supplier for it — and if you march under none, she will still pay a copper for the sketch.

choices.label: Commission gear in your colors (2 gold)
Let her sketch your kit for a copper

def.title: Beast Nest
notes: The old bow-or-beast pool produced a beast card about 93% of the time but a bow only about 57%; the authored beast door makes that promise 100%. Raid it is now free because a choice labeled as a raid should not quietly lose gold.
def.body: A trampled nest sits half-sunk in the Silt Hollows' mud, littered with the shed claws and feathers of something large. Everything worth carrying out of it is beast-work — fang, claw and hide, nothing else — if whatever built it doesn't come back and cost you a coin purse for the trouble.

def.title: The Bell Beneath the Ice
def.body: Beneath blue ice, a silver bell waits with its mouth turned toward the road. Its rim is warm. The metal seems to remember every hand that has tried to free it.

def.title: The Bell Beneath the Ice
def.body: Beneath blue ice, a silver bell waits with its mouth turned toward the road. Its rim is warm. The metal seems to remember every hand that has tried to free it.

def.title: The Broken Axle
def.body: A cart lies overturned on the Tolling Road, axle snapped clean through, goods scattered across the ruts. The driver begs anyone passing for a shoulder to right it, promising whatever thanks the wreck still holds — or, if you'd rather not strain yourself, just leave him to sort it out alone.

choices.label: Stay and salvage the wreckage properly (2 gold)

def.title: The Regrinding Wheel
def.body: Deep in the Cinderworks a bent-backed smith works a stone wheel taller than she is, sparks arcing in long white ribbons. "Five gold," she says without looking up, "and I'll regrind your gear into something properly better." Watch instead, and she won't even blink.

choices.label: Pay 5 gold to regrind your gear

def.title: The Regrinding Wheel
def.body: Deep in the Cinderworks a bent-backed smith works a stone wheel taller than she is, sparks arcing in long white ribbons. "Two gold," she says without looking up, "and I'll regrind your gear into something properly better." Watch instead, and she won't even blink.

choices.label: Pay 2 gold to regrind your gear

def.title: Circle of Adepts
def.body: Camped along the Muster Road, a circle of robed scholars debates arcane theory beneath a floating lattice of light. Two of their books are single-discipline and copied clean — one fire-work cover to cover, one lightning-work — and the third is the working grimoire, every discipline they practise jammed in together in no order at all. Copy from whichever you like; they're too deep in the argument to care.

def.title: Collapsed Barrow
def.body: A grave-mound in the Silt Hollows has slumped in on itself, exposing a narrow gap into the dark, silt-choked space below. Old barrows like this sometimes hold a forgotten trinket among the bones — and sometimes hold nothing but the bones themselves.

choices.label: Dig further for a real find (2 gold)
Seal it back up and move on

def.title: Crossroads Shrine
notes: The old shared pool offered 93% holy and 83% dark per offer; splitting it into separate 100% doors is a strict gain for both. Both choices remain two-gold, three-card offers so neither face dominates on width or price.
def.body: At the heart of the Crossroads Unquiet stands a weathered shrine, carvings split evenly between a rising sun and a crescent moon, and the two faces answer separately: tithe at the sun and what comes back is holy work, every time; scratch the moon-mark instead and it is dark work, every time. Others, less devout, simply pry the shrine apart for scrap.

choices.label: Scratch the moon-mark for dark work (2 gold)

def.title: The Ember Pit
notes: One merge door reached only 64.2% of runs and averaged 0.68 merges per run; adding this second door raises reach to 83.3% and the average to 1.32 without making the merge itself cost gold.
def.body: A pit of banked coals glows at the edge of the Cinderworks, deep enough to swallow a blade whole and hand it back changed — or hand back nothing, should the fire's mood sour. Thrust your gear in free and chance it, or pay the tender two gold for a safer cinder-gem instead. Three pieces of one grade, fed together, come back out as a single piece of the grade above — the tender lays out three the coals will take, and you choose.

choices.label: Thrust your gear into the coals
Pay 2 gold to steady the coals first
Feed three matched pieces to the coals

def.title: The Ember Pit
notes: 2026-09-26 T2: the mergeCards trio trade retired for new draws in favor of awardCardPoint (a free +1 stored tier-up point on one owned card) — version 1 stays live for any save with a pending trio already offered.
def.body: A pit of banked coals glows at the edge of the Cinderworks, deep enough to swallow a blade whole and hand it back changed — or hand back nothing, should the fire's mood sour. Thrust your gear in free and chance it, or pay the tender two gold for a safer cinder-gem instead. Feed one piece of your gear to the coals and it comes back a step further tempered toward its next grade — you choose which piece takes the heat.

choices.label: Thrust your gear into the coals
Pay 2 gold to steady the coals first
Feed one piece to the coals

def.title: The Factor's Ledger
notes: The goldSpent tally deliberately records aggregate commitment rather than purchase provenance. Twelve gold is the threshold, and the bounded payoff is one free gem choice.
def.body: A trade factor steps into the road with a ledger already open to your page. "Twelve gold and change, through the stalls and tolls of this road, by my count," she says, turning the book so you can see the tally — and it is your tally, coin for coin. "The road pays its regulars. One credit, one time. Spend it or tear the page."

def.title: Fence's Offer
def.body: A fence works a folding table at the shadowed edge of the Tolling Road, goods of dubious origin spread out under a stained cloth. "Coin, or a stone — your pick, no questions asked either way." She taps the table, already bored with the transaction.

def.title: Field Medic
def.body: A field medic has set up a triage tent at the roadside among the Muster Road's camps. Her herb satchel is sorted and green to the last cutting — nature work, all of it — while the rest of the tent is whatever keeps people upright: salves, wraps, mending songs, half-taught steadying tricks. Or, if none of it is what you need, she'll simply spare a little coin instead.

def.title: The Flaw-Finder
notes: This restores expose as an event-facing build door and supplies a second sellGem outlet. Four authored expose gems keep the offer viable even when the wave-one shop depth excludes the legendary option.
def.body: A jeweler's loupe glints from a stall no wider than its own strongbox on the Tolling Road. "Every stone has a flaw," its owner says, not as an apology — her whole tray is cut to FIND them, facets ground to open a weakness and hold it open. She buys as readily as she sells, if you are carrying a stone you are done with.

choices.label: Buy from the flaw-cut tray (2 gold)
Sell her a stone of your own

def.title: The Fortune-Teller
def.body: A veiled fortune-teller crouches at the crossroads shrine, cards fanned across a cracked marble slab, and offers a free reading of what's coming — the shrine only asks you trust what it shows. Cross her palm with silver instead, and she presses a smooth luck-stone into your hand.

def.title: The Gambler
notes: The two stakes are deterministic exchanges, two gold for three and five for nine, with costs paid up front. Walking away stays free so the event never becomes a gamble a broke player must take.
def.body: In the shadow of the crossroads shrine, a hooded figure shuffles cards at a folding table, coins stacked at her elbow, never once looking up as travelers pass. "Stake two gold on a safe cut," she says, "or five on a bold one — walk off with more than you sat down with, either way. Or don't play at all — some prefer to keep what little they have."

choices.label: Stake 2 gold on a safe cut
Stake 5 gold on a bold cut

def.title: Gemseller's Mishap
def.body: A peddler's cart hits a sinking rut at the edge of the Silt Hollows and her satchel bursts, scattering uncut gems across the mud. She scrambles after them, cursing — there's more here than she can gather alone, and more than a few have already rolled to rest against your boots.

def.title: Hermit's Riddle
def.body: On a mossy boulder overlooking the Hollow Yard, a hermit sits cross-legged, riddle already half-spoken before you've even stopped walking. Answer it right, she says, and you'll understand something about yourself no sparring ring could teach. Answer wrong, and you'll simply keep walking, no worse for it.

choices.label: Press her for a deeper truth (2 gold)

def.title: Overloaded Caravan
notes: The dedicated bow door replaces an old mixed offer that surfaced a bow only about 57% of the time, while the broad whole-book trunk remains available for players who want variety.
def.body: A merchant caravan sits axle-deep in the mud of the Tolling Road, its driver frantic as the sun sinks lower. A bundle of bowstaves is lashed to the tailgate where anyone can see it; the trunks behind it are packed with no order at all and could hold anything. Push, and she'll let you take from either — or just toss you a coin for a shoulder at the wheel.

choices.label: Take a bow off the tailgate (1 gold)
Push, then rummage the trunks (1 gold)

def.title: The Pyre-Watch
notes: The first lost life is the authored trigger. The event telegraphs the next omen, and its alms choice remains usable at any wallet so recovery is never gated by the defeat that unlocked it.
def.body: A watch-fire burns at the crossroads for the road's dead, tended by a hooded keeper who does not ask whose name you are carrying. The fire already knows: you left a life on a field behind you, and the pyre-watch keeps the old custom for anyone who limps past it — alms for the mourner, or arms for the living.

choices.label: Buy arms for the living (2 gold)
Let it burn, and walk on

def.title: Quartermaster's Error
def.body: A tired quartermaster at the edge of the Silt Hollows shoves a requisition ledger across the counter, muttering about a shipment that was never meant to reach you. "Take the armor plating — it's all defensive issue, wards and guards and nothing that hits back," he says, "or the loose gemstone in the corner. Don't care which — just take it and go before someone notices."

def.title: The Recruiter
notes: A guaranteed sword rack sits beside the mixed five-weapon cart, preserving the broad option while giving a committed sword build an honest routing choice.
def.body: A weapons broker flags you down from beneath a striped awning at the roadside edge of the Muster Road, arms full of blades and bowstrings still warm from the last camp. "Swords are racked on their own — anything else, you take your chances with what's in the cart," he grins, laying out a row of five either way. "Or take the coin instead. I won't haggle."

def.title: The Smith's Last Commission
def.body: At the Cinderworks' last working forge, an old smith banks her fire for good, hammer half-wrapped in oilcloth already. "Six gold," she offers, "for one more piece done right before I go." Decline, and she'll finish wrapping her tools and vanish into the dusk without you.

choices.label: Pay 6 gold for one last commission

def.title: The Smith's Last Commission
def.body: At the Cinderworks' last working forge, an old smith banks her fire for good, hammer half-wrapped in oilcloth already. "No charge," she offers, "for one more piece done right before I go." Decline, and she'll finish wrapping her tools and vanish into the dusk without you.

def.title: Ruined Anvil
notes: The zero-cost merge was added to an event that was already eligible at zero gold; the cards are the price. Keeping its catalog position unchanged preserves the seeded event sequence.
def.body: One of the Cinderworks' many forges stands half-collapsed and long abandoned, its anvil cracked but still serviceable. A rough blade sits cooling on the workbench, yours for the taking — or, for three gold toward proper tools, you could retemper it into something sturdier before you go. The anvil will still take a heavier job for nothing: lay three pieces of the SAME grade across it and they beat down into one piece of the next grade up, and the scrap left over decides which three you get to pick from.

choices.label: Beat three matched pieces into one

def.title: Ruined Anvil
notes: 2026-09-26 T2: the mergeCards trio trade retired for new draws in favor of awardCardPoint (a free +1 stored tier-up point on one owned card) — version 1 stays live for any save with a pending trio already offered.
def.body: One of the Cinderworks' many forges stands half-collapsed and long abandoned, its anvil cracked but still serviceable. A rough blade sits cooling on the workbench, yours for the taking — or, for three gold toward proper tools, you could retemper it into something sturdier before you go. The anvil will still take a heavier job for nothing: lay one piece of your gear across it and it beats down a step further along its own grade.

def.title: Sellsword Camp
def.body: A ring of tents and cookfires along the Muster Road marks a sellsword company between contracts. Their captain sizes you up and waves at the camp: the axes stand in their own rack by the mess tent, company-issue and nothing but axes, while the armory tent behind it is steel of every make thrown in together. Or, if you'd rather not linger, a coin for the road.

choices.label: Take a coin for the road

def.title: Sparring Circle
notes: The practice rack intentionally stays a broad mixed pool beside the paid lesson, and the free choice keeps the event usable when the player cannot afford training.
def.body: A ring of packed dirt marks the heart of the Hollow Yard, worn smooth by years of practice bouts. A scarred instructor waves you over: "Two gold buys you a real lesson. Or help yourself to the practice rack — it's every kind of gear anyone ever left here, all of it meant for hitting things, and no two pieces alike."

choices.label: Pay 2 gold for a real lesson
Help yourself to the mixed rack

def.title: The Sweep Drill
notes: Only one of the fifteen candidates in the old broad filter actually matched the promised splash lesson, roughly 7%; naming Shockwave Slam makes the lesson deterministic.
def.body: A grizzled instructor has cordoned off a stretch of the Hollow Yard for wide, sweeping cuts alone — the kind that catch whatever's standing next to your actual target, whether you meant it to or not. "Newer recruits call it splash," she snorts, resting a training axe on her shoulder. "I call it not missing twice. Two gold, and I'll teach you the sweep itself."

choices.label: Pay 2 gold to learn the sweep
Scavenge the practice yard for scraps

def.title: The Bell Unbound
def.body: In the Emberwaste the Frostmarch bell finally thaws. Steam curls from its silver throat, and it speaks the name you once gave it.

choices.label: Temper its Frost voice in the coals
Let it ring and walk away

def.title: The Land's Measure
notes: The local-work door follows the current biome's weapon lean and the hunter's kit follows its counter. Bow has no counter in the matchup table, so the safe coin choice remains the universal fallback.
def.body: A surveyor's drop-box juts from the mud of the Silt Hollows, stenciled with the mark of whatever country you are crossing. The locals cache what the land makes, and any land worth naming only makes one thing well — the box is local work to the last piece. Lashed underneath it rides a hunter's kit, picked to hurt what lives here. When anything can.

def.title: The Lapidary
notes: Selling a gem replaces the removed expose-filtered choice without stranding expose gems, which remain reachable through the Armory. Selling is free because surrendering the gem is already the price.
def.body: A lapidary has set up her wheel at the quiet end of the Cinderworks, trays of uncut facets sorted by what they promise rather than what they cost: a warding cut here, a cleansing cut there, a taunting cut that seems to want attention paid to it just for existing. "Reject bin's free to pick through," she says, without looking up, "and if you've got a stone you're done carrying, I'll take it off your hands too — fair price, no haggling." The good tray, though, isn't free.

choices.label: Pay 2 gold for a warding cut
Sell her a facet you're not using

def.title: The Reckoning
notes: Each payoff is gated by the shrine face that earned it and remains a free five-card offer. Defacing the shrine records the choice but intentionally summons neither face.
def.body: The shrine finds you, this time. A cairn of crossroads stone stands where no cairn stood yesterday, sun-mark and moon-mark cut fresh into its face — and beneath them, in scratches you never made, a tally of everything you ever left at the Crossroads Unquiet. Whatever keeps the shrine's accounts has ruled your devotion paid up, and tonight it settles its side of the ledger.

choices.label: Take the sun's settlement in holy work
Take the moon's settlement in dark work

def.title: The Second Toll
def.body: The bell you cut from the ice sounds once inside your pack, though nothing has touched it. Across the white distance, a cairn answers.

choices.label: Leave the bell at the cairn

def.title: The Thorn Garden Shrine
def.body: Deep in the Silt Hollows, a shrine has vanished beneath a decade of bramble growth, thorned vines lashed so thick across the stone that whatever it once honored is anyone's guess. What the tangle has swallowed is all armor-work — wards, guards, thorn-mail, nothing that hits back — worth the scratches, if you're willing to push through for it.

choices.label: Gather the fallen thorns at the edge
Leave the shrine to the thorns

def.title: Toll Bridge
notes: A guaranteed frost door sits beside the ninety-four-card broad pool at the same price and offer width, so the narrow route is an honest commitment rather than a tax.
def.body: A rickety toll bridge spans the worst of the Tolling Road's ravines, where the spray off the melt below freezes onto the ropes before it lands. Its keeper wants coin before he'll lower the gate, and he has two crates behind him: one is frost-work to the last piece, taken off the traders coming down from the pass, and the other is a jumble of whatever else he has confiscated, all of it made for hitting things. Refuse, and there's a longer, drier road around.

choices.label: Pay the toll, take the frost crate (2 gold)
Pay the toll, take the mixed crate (2 gold)

def.title: The Toll Collector's Ledger
def.body: A toll collector flags you down on the Tolling Road, ledger open, insisting a road tax is overdue for the wear you've caused passing through. Pay it and he waves you past with a stone from his confiscated crate — refuse, and he shrugs, scrawls something illegible, and lets you walk on regardless.

def.title: The Tutor's Return
notes: The first tutor visit is the paid setup; this free payoff is bounded once per run by the resolution gate and acknowledges the two gold already spent on the lesson.
def.body: You know the gnarled staff before you know the face: the old sellsword from the Hollow Yard, planted at the edge of the practice ring as if the two of you had set an appointment. "You paid for a lesson," she says. "You got half of one. I don't leave debts standing — mine or anybody's." The second half won't cost you a coin. Her sparring circle, though, still charges for the privilege.

choices.label: Take the second half of the lesson
Tell her the debt is settled

def.title: Two Ravens
def.body: Two ravens perch unnervingly still on the crossroads shrine's arms, and old omen-readers swear feeding them buys good fortune while ignoring them buys nothing at all. Toss them your scraps for a coin's trouble, or walk the long way around and let them watch you go.

choices.label: Walk the long way around, coin still in your pocket

def.title: The Venomer's Den
def.body: Off the Muster Road, half-hidden behind a curtain of hanging roots, a venomer keeps her still and her jars in careful rows, breath sharp with something that isn't quite smoke. "The weak batch is yours for nothing," she says, nodding at a dull green vial, "or two gold buys off the real shelf. Every jar on it does the one job — leaves whatever you use it on worse off than it started. Past that I make no promises about what's in the glass."

choices.label: Take the weak batch for free
Pay 2 gold for what she actually sells

def.title: Veteran's Last Lesson
def.body: At the far end of the Hollow Yard, a retiring blade-master sets down her practice cane and offers you her signature weapon, still humming faintly with old battles. "Take it, and carry what I built," she says, "or take my years instead — I've more use for rest now than for steel."

choices.label: Take her years of experience instead

def.title: Wandering Smith
def.body: Deep in the Cinderworks, a traveling smith works an anvil under a lean-to, hammer still ringing from the last commission. "Four gold," she grunts, "and I'll temper a blade proper — not the bronze rubbish you find lying about." Two gold, and you can have your pick of the pike-blanks stacked against the lean-to instead; she forges nothing else on spec, so lance-work is all that stack has ever been. Anything less, and she won't bother lighting the forge.

choices.label: Pay 4 gold for a properly tempered blade
Pick a lance-blank from the stack (2 gold)

def.title: The Wandering Tutor
def.body: The dust of the Hollow Yard has barely settled from the last duel when an old sellsword rises to meet you, gnarled staff in hand. "Two gold," she says, "and I'll show you where you're wasting your strength." Her lesson won't be free — but it won't be forgotten, either.

def.title: The Weighing Stone
def.body: A black basalt stone squats at the crossroads' heart, said to weigh a traveler's resolve at a glance. Press your palm to it and it may show a glimpse of arms you'll carry — or leave your hand simply cold. Others just skirt around it, unwilling to let a stone judge them.

choices.label: Press your palm to the stone

def.title: The Roadside Wager
def.body: A drill instructor at the practice yard slaps a coin on the rail: stake it against your own form, and you might walk off richer — or just walk off.

def.title: Cold Iron Drill
def.body: A sergeant drills recruits through iron forms at the yard's edge. Two gold buys a place in the line and a weapon fresh off the rack; free, you can only watch from the fence.

def.title: The Underdog's Stand
def.body: Word spreads fast when the road costs a life. A company of stubborn holdouts waves you over, offering to beat three matched pieces of your gear into something that might hold better next time.

def.title: The Underdog's Stand
def.body: Word spreads fast when the road costs a life. A company of stubborn holdouts waves you over, offering to beat one piece of your gear into something that might hold better next time.

def.title: Veteran's Wisdom
def.body: Three wins in, and the yard's old veterans finally wave you into their circle. What they teach next won't come from any drill.

def.title: Crooked Dice
def.body: A gambler beneath the crossroads shrine rattles a cup of black dice, promising the road pays double to the bold — or nothing at all to the unlucky.

def.title: Silent Augury
def.body: A hush falls at the crossroads shrine as an augur reads smoke rising off cold coals — a glimpse of the road ahead, if you'll trade a moment's patience for it.

def.title: The Hanged Stranger
def.body: A stranger hangs a lantern at the shrine's foot, trading omens for anything bright you're willing to part with.

def.title: The Last Omen's Toll
def.body: Word of your first felled champion reaches the shrine before you do. The omen-readers already have your fortune half-drawn.

def.title: The Quiet Muster
def.body: A quiet muster gathers off the road's shoulder, support-hands and menders comparing notes over a cookfire. Two gold buys a seat at their circle.

def.title: Banner of Five
def.body: Two wins in and a recruiter's banner catches your eye — five weapons laid out for anyone who's proven they can use one.

fixed.label: Take a toast and a coin

def.title: The Sworn Company
def.body: A sworn company drills three-deep at the roadside, offering to beat your gear together the way they beat their ranks into shape.

def.title: The Sworn Company
def.body: A sworn company drills three-deep at the roadside, offering to temper one piece of your gear the way they beat their own ranks into shape.

def.title: Temper or Break
def.body: A forge-hand offers to temper your gear over open coals — three gold gets you a real chance at something better, or nothing but scorch marks.

def.title: Temper or Break
def.body: A forge-hand offers to temper your gear over open coals — three gold gets you a real chance at something better, or nothing but scorch marks.

def.title: The Scrap Reclaimer
def.body: A reclaimer picks through scrap at the forge's edge, trading facets no one else wants for the ones that ward, cleanse, and taunt.

fixed.label: Trade a stone of your own

def.title: The Capstone Reforge
def.body: Two champions felled, and the master forge itself opens to you — one true piece of your kit, reforged past its old limit.

def.title: The Toll of Plenty
def.body: A tollkeeper on the Tolling Road offers a wager instead of a toll: stake five gold and the gate might swing wide with more than you paid — or simply take your coin and go.

def.title: The Quiet Ledger
def.body: A quiet ledger-keeper flags you down before the next stall. Eight gold through her books earns a courtesy the regulars get.

def.title: Sellsword's Bazaar
def.body: A bazaar stall at the market's edge sells warding charms to anyone passing, one gold and no haggling.

def.title: The Silt Reliquary
def.body: A half-sunk reliquary in the Silt Hollows holds three matched relics, ready to be beaten into one truer piece.

def.title: The Silt Reliquary
def.body: A half-sunk reliquary in the Silt Hollows holds one true relic, waiting to be beaten a step further.

def.title: The Hollow Stash
def.body: A hollow stash beneath a fallen log holds mender's tools, worth two gold to whoever digs it out properly.

def.title: The Forgotten Ledger
def.body: A forgotten ledger surfaces from an old cache, its pages full of every road you've already walked.

def.title: The Bandit's Toll
def.body: A ragged band blocks the road, spears low and grins lower. Their captain names a toll in gold — or, failing that, in blood. Either way, they say, you are paying something before you pass.

def.title: The Arena Pit
def.body: A sunken ring of packed earth waits behind a curtain of oiled canvas, ringed by a crowd that has already placed its bets. The pit-master waves you toward the rope. "Tougher bout, tougher purse," he says, and grins at the fighter already stretching in the sand.

def.title: The Champion's Duel
def.body: A traveling champion plants a banner at the crossroads and calls out anyone who thinks their steel is worth testing. The crowd that gathers already knows this one is no easy bout — but a champion's duel tempers whatever you carry into it.

def.title: The Barrow Guardian
def.body: The cairn stones over this barrow have been disturbed, and something under them has noticed. It rises slow and huge from the broken earth, hoard-marks still ground into its knuckles — whatever it was set to guard, it means to keep guarding.

def.title: The Sellswords' Wager
def.body: A band of sellswords has pooled a purse and is offering it to anyone who can put their toughest down. Odds are chalked on a barrel head, and the crowd is already loud about which way they think this goes.

def.title: The Duskroad Challenger
def.body: A masked figure waits where the road dims toward dusk, testing every traveler who passes with the same plain offer: a fair fight, a fair prize, no names asked either way.

def.title: Feathered Cairn
def.body: A low cairn of arrow-marked stones stands beside the road. Black feathers turn in the wind around a set of deliberate cuts, each one pointing toward a fork you cannot yet see.

def.title: Feathered Cairn
def.body: A low cairn of arrow-marked stones stands beside the road. Black feathers turn in the wind around a set of deliberate cuts, each one pointing toward a fork you cannot yet see.

def.title: Far Sight
def.body: At the next omen-stone, the cairn's cuts return in the dust. They trace a safer fork ahead, with one loose mark pointing toward a small hidden cache.

def.title: Far Sight
def.body: At the next omen-stone, the cairn's cuts return in the dust. They trace a safer fork ahead, with one loose mark pointing toward a small hidden cache.

def.title: Fletcher's Tithe
def.body: A fletcher's stall stands unmanned at an Arrowfell crossroads, its ledger open to a page marked "tithe." One fine arrow rests beside it, already fletched for a hand that never came to claim it.

fixed.label: Pay the tithe with your absence

def.title: Gilded Detour
def.body: A broker's bright pavilion blocks the road. The richest travelers are invited to turn a little fortune into something rarer.

def.title: Gilded Detour
def.body: A broker's bright pavilion blocks the road. The richest travelers are invited to turn a little fortune into something rarer.

def.title: Victor's Table
def.body: Veterans from many roads raise their cups as you pass. Five victories earn a place beside them and first choice of the spoils.

def.title: Bitter Rematch
def.body: Word of your answered defeat reaches a scarred training yard. Your old rival's mark hangs beside the card that ended the rematch.

def.title: Last Light at Road's End
def.body: After the last defeat, a lone lantern burns where the road divides. Its keeper offers strength for the safer path—or a spark for the unlit one.

def.title: The Unlit Road
def.body: The lantern's spark reveals a hidden mile between the known roads. It offers one last cache before the darkness closes again.

def.title: Mirror of the Board
def.body: A road-forge holds a mirror wide enough for your whole formation. It reflects a single shared purpose more clearly than any face.

def.title: Beyond the Board's Mirror
def.body: The reflection returns at another forge, still holding the affinity it witnessed. One final transformation waits behind the silvered road.

def.title: The Card That Remembered
def.body: One skill has followed your victories and struck the final blow against a great foe. At a roadside shrine, the card begins to remember more than ink.

def.title: The Remembered Art
def.body: At the next forge, the bound card names the victories that shaped it. Its answer is a final refinement—or permission to rest.

def.title: Cartographer's Missing Road
def.body: A cartographer compares your traveled lands to a map with one deliberate blank. The absent road points toward a biome you have not yet crossed.

def.title: The Missing Road
def.body: The cartographer's mark appears beneath your feet in the biome it named. For a moment, the road opens onto a cache hidden outside every common map.

def.title: The Broker's Scale
def.body: A broker has set her scale up at the crossroads, weighing coin against whatever the road has worn thin — a limb still healing, an edge gone dull. She never carries the same goods twice, but she is never far from the road either, and her prices climb a little with every trade she strikes.

def.title: The Old Duelist's Grip
def.body: A retired duelist rests at the roadside, turning a nicked practice blade over in weathered hands. He watches your stance more than your face, and after a long moment he holds the blade out hilt-first. "Grip's the whole art," he says. "Yours could stand to learn it."

def.title: The Standing Stone
def.body: A weathered stone leans at the crossroads, worn smooth by hands that pressed against it long before yours. The old markings promise nothing you can read, but the stone is warm under your palm — warmer than the air around it, as though it has been waiting.

fixed.label: Press your palm to the stone

def.title: A Smith's Tempering
def.body: Sparks scatter from a wayside forge as a smith works a plate of scarred steel, quenching it again and again until it rings true. She catches you watching and nods toward your own gear. "Bring it here," she says. "One more pass never hurt anyone who lived to need it."

def.title: Names Under Stone
def.body: Beyond Duskbarrow's fallen lord, a mile of grave markers leans toward the road. One stone speaks a name that only a bearer of dark craft could answer.

def.title: The Grave Answers
def.body: Three roads later, the stolen silver rings against a nameless marker. The earth answers in a voice that has followed beneath every mile.

def.title: The Last Acolyte
def.body: A cloaked figure kneels at the edge of Duskbarrow's rot, the only living student of a dead order. They offer to teach you the rite they alone remember, in exchange for a place on your road.

fixed.label: Leave the acolyte to the rot

def.title: Grave-Wax Seals
def.body: Three seals of black grave-wax lie unbroken in a crumbled niche, each stamped with a mark that only a dark-tempered hand can read.

def.title: Cinderheart Crucible
def.body: A smith tends the last furnace between Emberwaste and the road beyond. It wakes only for flame proven in gold or carried through a fallen tyrant.

def.title: The Ash Oracle
def.body: An oracle sits cross-legged in the Emberwaste's drifting soot, reading futures out of the way embers curl and die. She presses a warm brand into your palm before you have asked a single question.

def.title: Slag-Glass Cache
def.body: Fused slag has cooled into a glassy shell around a hoard from some earlier traveler, its contents visible but sealed. Only fire-tempered hands can crack it open.

def.title: Whiteout Pilgrim
def.body: A pilgrim steps out of the Frostmarch white, following a road visible only to those who have won beneath frost's banner.

def.title: The Pilgrim's Marker
def.body: A white-road marker rises where the storm should have erased every trail. The pilgrim's sign points through the safest break in the gale.

def.title: Rime-Locked Sledge
def.body: A frost-smith's sledge lies half-forged in a block of ice at the Frostmarch's edge, its head shaped for a binding cold that never finished setting.

def.title: Hoarfrost Reliquary
def.body: A traveling reliquary keeper has set up a stall of frost-worked wares between two dead pines, each piece rimed white and humming faintly with cold.

def.title: The Sanctum Vigil
def.body: Past Hallowfield's consecrated line, a keeper still holds a vigil no map explains. The ward has stood since before the road, and it has never once let anything back out.

def.title: What the Ward Kept Out
def.body: The vigil answers: a wisp of dark magic, held at the boundary since long before you crossed it, still restless against the consecrated line. The keeper offers you the choosing of what becomes of it.

fixed.label: Let it rest behind the ward

def.title: Penitent's Road
def.body: A stretch of Hallowfield's road runs bare of grass, worn smooth by knees rather than boots. At its end a plain altar holds one blade of consecrated light, left for whoever finishes the walk.

def.title: Moon-Scented Trail
def.body: Silver tracks cross the Howlmoor road and vanish into heather. The trail bends for a hunter who runs with beasts—or has already broken a pack.

def.title: The Moon Hunt
def.body: The silver trail reaches its quarry beneath a low moon. Hunter and hunted wait for you to decide how the chase ends.

def.title: The Howling Cairn
def.body: A cairn of bleached bone and antler stands where Howlmoor's packs gather at dusk, a single fanged trophy wedged into its crown for whoever can call the howl back.

def.title: The Red Standard
def.body: An old Ironmoot standard hangs above a silent drill yard. Three victories won beneath the axe are stitched into its ragged edge.

def.title: Blood-Price Muster
def.body: An Ironmoot recruiter has nailed a muster notice to a splintered post: axes wanted, blood-price paid in kind. A single notched blade hangs beneath it, already claimed by no one.

def.title: The Whetting Pit
def.body: A stone pit worn smooth by generations of axe-edges sits at Ironmoot's heart, its grindstones still turning under no visible hand.

fixed.label: Set an edge against the grindstones

def.title: The Last Hedge
def.body: At Pikewold's far boundary, a veteran holds the last living hedge with one weathered lance and a lesson in refusing the road's advance.

def.title: The Pike-Forge
def.body: A field-forge still glows at Pikewold's rear line, its bellows worked by no one and its rack holding a single braced shaft, cooling from the last quench.

def.title: Drill-Sergeant's Chest
def.body: A locked chest sits at the foot of a drill yard long since abandoned, stamped with a dead sergeant's seal and heavy with a lance-hand's due.

def.title: Thunder in a Bottle
def.body: A Stormreach tinker has trapped the echo of your swiftest lightning victory. The bottle shakes whenever the road turns toward another fight.

def.title: The Lightning-Struck Spire
def.body: A shattered spire juts from Stormreach's ridgeline, its stone still smoking from a strike that split it top to base. A single blackened arc still crawls the crack, waiting for a hand that can hold it.

def.title: The Capacitor Vault
def.body: A tinker's vault hums behind a door of copper and glass, charged decades ago and never discharged. Only a lightning-tempered hand can draw on it without earthing the whole store.

def.title: The Garrison's Oath
def.body: Swornhold's drill yard still musters at the old hours. Two victories won under its banner earn a place in the line — and the oath that comes with it.

def.title: The Oath Kept
def.body: Word of the oath reaches you again, three roads on: the garrison held its line without you, and the standard-bearer sends word of what your name still earns there.

def.title: The Oathsmith
def.body: Swornhold's forge never truly cools. Its smith takes no coin, only oaths, and the blade she sets aside today is already promised to whoever swears to carry it into the line.

def.title: Bloom Behind the Teeth
def.body: Past Thornwild's poisoned crown, a flower opens inside the jaw of a stone beast. It knows the nature-bound hand that carried venom through a ruler's fall.

def.title: The Rootbound Hermit
def.body: A hermit sits half-grown into Thornwild's tangle, bark climbing one arm and thorns threading through their hair. They offer to walk with you, if you'll carry the thorn they can no longer wield.

def.title: The Seedvault
def.body: A stone vault stands sealed beneath Thornwild's oldest tree, its lid grown shut with roots. Inside, a keeper's hoard of seeds waits for a nature-tempered hand to crack it open.
